# Pinned a64js runtime

Imported from the existing `disass_arm/third_parts/a64js` checkout at Git commit `aa0e547ca5313779c87e1e52d75687b12e985615`. The tracked worktree was clean when imported; the exact imported file contents, not just the commit, are identified by SHA-256 in `snapshot.json`. No runtime dependency on that checkout remains.

`LICENSE` is the upstream MIT license and copyright notice. No XML reference data, download/archive, generator, tests, CLI, package manager files or `node_modules` are bundled here.

This is a **transformed runtime snapshot**, not an unchanged source copy. TypeScript 5.9.3 `transpileModule` (target ES2023, module ESNext, `verbatimModuleSyntax: true`) erased types; an AST transform changed static import/export `.ts` specifiers to `.js`. Runtime dependencies were followed transitively from upstream `src/decode.ts` and `src/format.ts`. All 1,918 reachable runtime modules are needed by those roots, including the statically imported generated encoding inventory. Optional formatting is retained because decoding and operand construction share upstream formatter-family code.

`snapshot.json` records the original TS SHA-256 and emitted JS SHA-256 for every imported runtime module. Upstream `types.ts` and `operand-types.ts` are preserved as declarations with the same AST specifier rewrite and have their own source/output hashes. `decode.d.ts` and `format.d.ts` are small local API declarations matching the upstream public signatures; their hashes are separately recorded. No generated instructions or decode logic were hand-patched. First-party completion and structured-operand adaptation live in `src/decoders/arm64`, not here.

To update, select/review the upstream revision and actual worktree contents, repeat the recorded AST/transpilation process over the runtime dependency closure, preserve the license, regenerate source/output hashes, and run the ARM decoder behavioral tests plus the compiled loader/decoder smoke through the integration owner. Do not regenerate tables using a different Arm release as an incidental vendoring step. Vendored JS is copied by TypeScript's `allowJs` with `checkJs: false`; first-party TypeScript strictness remains unchanged.
